assertions.description: fail has two operators; warn survives, so hasBands() stays true
assertions.reason: fail has 2 operators (gt, lt) — exactly one is allowed — so this rule declares a limit it cannot apply, and would report PASS without ever testing fail

assertions.description: a tolerance of 20 meant as 20% — nothing is negative
assertions.reason: fail can never fire: < -19 ms is unreachable because this metric is never negative. The rule reports PASS on every run, including one that measured nothing at all. A tolerance meant as a percentage is written as a fraction — 0.2, not 20.

assertions.description: meant never gates; ignoring it leaves a rule that gates
assertions.reason: "observe" is no longer a rule modifier. It meant "report this and never gate", and a rule that keeps its bands without it does gate — so leaving it in place would silently invert what the rule was written to do. Delete the bands to stop the rule judging, or delete "observe" to let it judge.

assertions.description: meant fail-if-absent; ignoring it turns a red build green
assertions.reason: "onMissing" is no longer a rule modifier. A target that matches nothing is now NOT_JUDGED / NO_MATCH and never fails the run on its own, because a plan running a subset is legitimate — so a rule relying on "onMissing": "fail" would pass where it used to fail. Delete the key; if a missing sampler must stop the build, assert on it in the pipeline.

assertions.description: a corridor is two rules now
assertions.reason: fail outside is no longer an operator. A corridor is two rules: one with "lt" at the low bound and one with "gt" at the high bound. Written that way each says which end was missed, and each reports how far past its own limit the run was. — so this rule declares a limit it cannot apply, and would report PASS without ever testing fail
